subject: Renewal: Dedicated GPU runway & Q3–Q4 throughput sensitivity
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@opengrid.ai>, OpenGrid Procurement <procurement@opengrid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated GPU runway & Q3–Q4 throughput sensitivity

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the productive renewal kickoff this week. Per our conversation I put together a short QPS/token runway and a conservative GPU recommendation for your Dedicated pool to cover the Q3–Q4 forecast you shared. I attached a CSV with the quarter-by-quarter projection and a short PDF with the recommended configuration.

High-level summary:
- Baseline workload (current production): ~450 QPS sustained, ~75M tokens/day.
- Projected growth (conservative): 30% Q3, then 25% Q4, driven by onboarding two new partners and increased inference for interactive features.
- Recommended reserved capacity for 12-month renewal term: 10 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool, with a 20% burst buffer (ephemeral burst instances) for peak campaigns.
- Rationale: this configuration preserves 95th percentile latency under 450–550ms for your 99% interactive SLO while keeping unit token cost within your target band.

Attachments: opengrid_qps_projection_2027Q3Q4.csv (CSV), redwood_gpu_recommendation_v2.pdf (PDF).

Two asks:
1) Can procurement confirm target renewal cadence and preferred contract start date (we proposed 2027-09-01)?
2) Would you like a quick sensitivity table showing 8 / 10 / 12 GPU scenarios with cost delta and expected 99th-latency impact? I can get that back by Tuesday.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through the numbers.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@opengrid.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: OpenGrid Procurement <procurement@opengrid.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated GPU runway & Q3–Q4 throughput sensitivity

Jonas — thank you for the detailed packet and projections. Procurement looped me in with timelines; they need an internal cost/benefit to present to the Cloud Ops budget board next Friday.

Quick clarifying questions before we take this to budget:
- Can you provide a firm SLA / throughput guarantee for the 10-GPU reserved pool (what does Redwood commit to for sustained QPS and 99th latency under the recommended config)?
- We need a clear comparison of the expected token/unit cost at 8 vs 10 vs 12 GPUs (including the cost of burst capacity). Please show absolute $/1M tokens and delta vs current term.
- Any constraints on rolling upgrades during the contract term? We have planned model changes in Oct that may shift memory needs.

Procurement asked if Redwood can push a redlined term sheet by next Wednesday (2027-07-21) so they can start drafting the internal approval.

Thanks — Asha
Asha Patel
Director, Platform Engineering — OpenGrid
asha.patel@opengrid.ai

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated GPU runway & Q3–Q4 throughput sensitivity

Asha / Jonas — looping in Ben to make sure ops and pricing are aligned. I reviewed Jonas' projections and ran a short sensitivity sweep against their traffic shape. Summary below and attached the recommendation PDF with scenario pricing: redwood_gpu_recommendation_v2.pdf.

Scenario summary (99th latency target = 750ms interactive, cost = $/1M tokens):
- 8 GPUs reserved: hits budget floor but 99th jumps to ~1.2s under 35% growth spikes — not recommended if you need interactive SLAs.
- 10 GPUs reserved (Jonas' baseline): steady for conservative growth up to 30% with 20% burst; estimated $/1M tokens = $320 (baseline current: $365).
- 12 GPUs reserved: provides comfortable headroom for model changes in Oct, 99th stays <700ms under 45% growth; estimated $/1M tokens = $365.

Operational notes:
- Burst pool will be ephemeral preemptible instances; cost for burst usage is tracked separately and capped per month in the proposed contract.
- Rolling upgrades: we recommend a canary rollout and a staged model swap scheduled during low-traffic windows; no hard constraint but we ask 72h notice for major architecture changes that change memory footprint.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jonas — send the 8/10/12 GPU cost delta table as a single CSV for procurement.
2) Asha — confirm that procurement wants the contract to start 2027-09-01 or another date.
3) Ben — can you confirm whether we can include a 10% concession on the first 3 months' invoice if they commit to 12 GPUs for 12 months?

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

> On Tue, Jul 13, 2027 at 11:03 AM Asha Patel <asha.patel@opengrid.ai> wrote:
> > (Questions inline)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: OpenGrid renewal — sensitivity + pricing ask

Team — quick internal runbook based on replies from Asha / procurement. I attached the CSV projection earlier; below is the ask and recommended posture.

- Procurement needs: 8 / 10 / 12 GPU cost table (absolute $/1M tokens + delta), and a firm statement from us on what we can guarantee for sustained QPS at 99th latency for the 10-GPU configuration.
- Ops constraints: Ben, confirm we can offer a <=750ms 99th latency guarantee for sustained 500 QPS on 10 GPUs given their model profile (medium context length, kv-cache friendly). If not, flag the expected delta and whether 12 is the minimum.
- Commercial concession: Marissa suggested 10% off first 3 months if they commit to 12 GPUs. I propose we present two offer tiers to procurement: (A) 10 GPUs reserved + 20% burst (standard price), (B) 12 GPUs reserved + 10% first-3-month concession (preferred).

If Ops can certify the 10-GPU sustained numbers, I think we move procurement toward the 10→12 tradeoff and let them choose based on budget board. Timeline: need the cost CSV and the ops confirmation by EOD Wed (2027-07-21).

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
